confirmed: Source checked independently: the complete journal abstract from Crossref, corroborated by OpenAlex W7202073024 and Semantic Scholar paper 3e1cb674b5204879801a3b3e2f67ddb8fcd14bfb. No local markdown or PDF is recorded (retrieval.json, c113: not_obtained); the publisher HTML and PDF URLs both returned HTTP 403. No full text or appendices were read.

source.version accurately limits the original screening to an abstract. Crossref metadata confirms the title, all four listed authors, Architecture volume 6, issue 3, page/article 133, and publication date 2026-08-10 (Crossref DOI record: title, author, volume, issue, page, published).

The described study is a within-student sequence from handmade concept to AI refinement, explicitly termed observational; no randomized assignment of people to AI assistance is described. quasi_people, assignment.randomized = no, and observational context are supported for the study described in the accessible abstract (Crossref abstract, opening methods and final limitation sentence).

The reported cohort comprises 45 first-year students, who developed bus-stop designs and then reworked them with AI visualisation tools. This is a count of people, with the same cohort at both stages, and is below 50; no randomized count or attrition details are supplied (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "In a first-year studio").

Creativity is scored on produced designs by experts using the same nine-dimensional Consensual Assessment Technique rubric before and after AI refinement, satisfying the output-scoring criterion (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "Pre-AI and post-AI designs").
S1-O1 reported values and the one-line finding match the abstract exactly: total creativity 3.38 to 3.71; Wilcoxon p = 0.022, dz = 0.38 (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "Results suggest").

S1-O2 reported changes match exactly: functional adequacy +0.80, structural feasibility +0.78, and environmental response +0.56; the abstract calls these increases significant (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "Results suggest").
S1-O3 reflects the abstract wording that novelty dimensions remained unaltered; no dimension-specific novelty numbers are printed there (Crossref abstract, sentence beginning "Results suggest").

The accessible source describes an empirical studio study, not a synthesis; no study pool, pooled estimate, or pooled interval is reported. Core exclusion is supported by the observational design and reported cohort below 50 (Crossref abstract, methods and final limitation sentence).
summary: The accessible Crossref abstract supports a non-randomized, within-student study with a reported cohort of 45 and matches every reported result number. Three corrections concern unverified analyzed counts, separately scored appropriateness dimensions, and missing statistic-availability labels; the publisher full text was inaccessible, so no PDF or appendix audit was possible.
